defects.claim: selectionRegion ignores consuming ancestors, so a consumed (never drawn) child yields a selection export region
defects.scenario: select an operand of a boolean/compound node (reachable by entering it: `enteredGroup.isEnterable` allows consumesChildren). The operand is never painted on its own; `sceneContentBounds` excludes such nodes (`consumed`, contentBounds.ts:36). selectionRegion returns the operand's full drawn box, so an intersect/subtract result exports with a region framing ink that is not there (or a result that draws nothing exports as non-null). Expected: the operand treated like other undrawn nodes (or mapped to its consuming ancestor).

defects.claim: A selected parent's drawn bounds include annotation-layer descendants that export excludes, enlarging the crop
Strict PNG export validates the warmup plan's diagnostics, not the final plan's, so losses introduced after warmup go unreported
selectionRegion omits the copies a selected container draws via copiesFromPose, so the exported crop cuts them off
defects.scenario: select a symmetry group (a container with `copiesFromPose`) and export the selection as PNG/SVG/PDF. `boxOf` answers `drawnAabbOf` of the group, which unions its members' boxes but never carries them through the copies (drawnBounds.ts `inkExtentsOf` has no copy step). The region is the original's box only, so every mirrored/rotated copy outside it is cut off. `sceneContentBounds` (core/canvas/contentBounds.ts:38-44) answers the same "what does this draw" question with `copiesWithin` and covers the copies — two answers to one decision.
defects.cause: copies not carried into selection bounds

defects.claim: shownIds recurses into children of a consumesChildren node on a hidden or annotation layer, counting ones the render walk never paints
defects.scenario: a boolean/compound node (`consumesChildren: true`) sits on a hidden layer (or an annotation layer) and is selected. `shown` replaces it with `doc.childrenOf(id).flatMap(shown)`, so its operands' boxes become the region, though the walk draws neither the node nor its operands (`buildSceneTree` gives a consuming node no children; `sceneContentBounds` contentBounds.ts:33 and `paintedMembers` drawnBounds.ts:108 both return [] here). Expected `null` / "draws nothing"; got a region over undrawn operands, exporting an empty or wrong image. The same "what does a hidden-layer node draw" rule is answered three ways.

defects.claim: selectionRegion treats a zero-width or zero-height region as drawing something, so the PNG export then refuses it
defects.scenario: select only a straight horizontal (or vertical) path with no stroke, or any node whose drawn box is degenerate on one axis. `unionAabb` returns a box with `height: 0`, so `selectionRegion` returns a region rather than `null`, and `selectionRegionSource` does not raise its "draws nothing" error. `exportRegions(scene, selectionRegionsSource(ids), 'png')` then reaches `planPixelRender`, whose `checkPixelRenderRect` throws `renderSceneToPixels: sourceRect.height must be a positive finite number, got 0`. Expected: either `null` / the "draws nothing" error that the doc promises for a selection drawing nothing, or a region the formats accept.
defects.cause: degenerate box not treated as empty

defects.claim: Dev 'unread option' warning is suppressed for an override of the same format id that reads different options
defects.scenario: `exportRegions(scene, r, 'png', { dpi: 2 })` warns once and records `png\0dpi`. A consumer then registers its own `png` format declaring `options: []` (or a different set), or disposes it and the built-in reappears; a later misspelled/unsupported `dpi` passed to the new format is never warned about, because the dedupe key is the id, not the format object whose `options` decided the warning. Keyed by format (e.g. a WeakMap<ExportFormat, Set<string>>) each registration would warn for itself.
defects.cause: dedupe keyed by id rather than the format registered
